## 🦆 Join DataFrames with SQL — `query_df`

You've loaded a few DataFrames (from Athena, S3, DynamoDB, ...). Now you need to **combine** them — a join, a group-by, a window. Instead of chaining `pd.merge` + `groupby` + `rename`, write the **SQL** and let `query_df` run it with **DuckDB in-process**.

- Reference each DataFrame **by its variable name** — nothing to register.
- Runs entirely in the VM against the frames already in memory: **no AWS call, no network**.
- Returns a new DataFrame; your inputs are untouched.

| Stage | Helper | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Load | `read_athena` / `read_s3` / `read_dynamodb` | pull each table into a DataFrame |
| Combine | `query_df("SELECT ... FROM a JOIN b ...")` | SQL across the frames by name |
| Chart | `plot_bar` / `plot_pie` / `plot_corr` | one-line view of the result |

```mermaid
graph LR
  A["frame_a (read_*)"] --> Q["query_df (DuckDB in-process)"]
  B["frame_b (read_*)"] --> Q
  Q --> R["result DataFrame"]
  R --> V["plot_* / profile"]
```

For warehouse-scale SQL (pushdown to the engine) keep using `read_athena` / `read_aurora`; `query_df` is for frames you ALREADY have in memory. `duckdb` is baked into the image — nothing to install. Replace the `<...>` placeholders.

# 1) Load the frames you want to combine. Any readers work — the point is you end
#    up with 2+ DataFrames in your namespace. Give them clear variable names:
#    those names become the TABLE names in your SQL.
orders   = read_athena("SELECT * FROM <orders_table> LIMIT 5000")
products = read_s3("s3://<bucket>/<products.parquet>")
print("orders:", orders.shape, "· products:", products.shape)

# 2) Combine with SQL — reference each frame by its variable name. DuckDB speaks
#    standard SQL (joins, GROUP BY, window functions, CTEs). This runs in-process
#    over the in-memory frames: no re-query, no pandas merge chain.
summary = query_df('''
    SELECT p.<category_col>              AS category,
           COUNT(*)                     AS orders,
           ROUND(SUM(o.<revenue_col>), 2) AS revenue
    FROM orders o
    JOIN products p ON o.<product_id> = p.<id>
    GROUP BY p.<category_col>
    ORDER BY revenue DESC
''')
summary

# 3) Chart the result with a one-line helper (dark theme + auto-display baked in).
plot_bar(summary, x="category", y="revenue", title="Revenue by Category")
